extracted.intended_audience: general readers, TV viewers, entertainment reporters, and researchers interested in the TV series Roseanne and its reception
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and measures used in the article to describe and assess the Roseanne television series (revival and original run), including critical reception, ratings, awards, distribution, and controversy-driven production decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rotten Tomatoes approval and consensus
rubrics_metrics.description: Rotten Tomatoes approval rating of 69% based on 80 reviews, with an average rating of 6.72/10. The website consensus reads: "Roseanne's return finds the show's classic format, original cast, and timely humor intact, even if the latest batch of episodes suffers from sporadically uneven execution."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses aggregated critic reviews to evaluate a season along dimensions such as preservation of classic format, presence of original cast, timeliness of humor, and consistency of execution. Percent approval and average numeric rating are reported; the textual 'consensus' highlights strengths and weaknesses critics noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Metacritic weighted average
rubrics_metrics.description: Metacritic assigned the season a score of 69 out of 100 based on 31 reviews, indicating "generally favorable reviews."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weighted-average critic score (Metascore) used as an overall quality indicator; number of reviews and Metacritic's qualitative banding (e.g., 'generally favorable') provide context for the numeric value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Viewership ratings and time-shifted metrics (Nielsen, Live+3/Live+7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Nielsen ratings and time-shifted viewing metrics are used to measure popularity: e.g., the revival premiere was seen by 18.45 million live and same-day viewers, gained an additional 6.59 million via Live+3 (and 2.2 million more over the following four days), totaling 27.26 million overall — a record Live+7 gain. Seasons are ranked in Nielsen season averages and historical top-5/top-10 placements are reported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates a show's success by raw viewer counts, Nielsen season ranking, and growth from delayed viewing windows (Live+3, Live+7). Emphasizes that time-shifted metrics can dramatically change a program's perceived reach and set records independent of live numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry awards and nominations
rubrics_metrics.description: Awards and nominations are presented as markers of critical/industry recognition: e.g., Emmy wins (Roseanne Barr and Laurie Metcalf), Golden Globe wins (Barr and John Goodman), a Peabody Award (1992), People's Choice Awards, and a total of 27 Emmy nominations (including the revival) though never nominated for Best Comedy Series.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wins and nominations (Emmys, Golden Globes, Peabody, People's Choice) are used to indicate peer/industry esteem and historic significance; specific performer and series-level awards are cited to demonstrate critical acclaim even when some major categories (like Best Comedy Series) were never attained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cancellation and creator public conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: ABC canceled the revival and reversed renewal after Roseanne Barr posted a widely criticized racially insensitive tweet about Valerie Jarrett; network leadership described the remarks as "abhorrent, repugnant and inconsistent with our values." Episodes and the series were pulled from streaming/cable lineups following the controversy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrates that a creator's public conduct and controversial statements are a production-level criterion that can override ratings and awards: networks may cancel, remove content from distribution, suspend awards campaigns, and cause talent to dissociate. Ethical/professional standards and corporate values therefore factor into whether a show continues to air or be distributed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Syndication, carriage, and availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Off-network syndication history and platform availability are tracked (e.g., TBS, Nick at Nite, TV Land, Oxygen, later Cozi TV; availability on Amazon Prime Video, Hoopla, Pluto TV). The article also records removal from Hulu and Viacom networks concurrent with ABC's cancellation and later returns to some networks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Long-term popularity and cultural footprint are assessed by syndication pickups, platform availability, and whether networks continue to carry reruns. Removal from platforms after controversies is noted as an indicator of reputational and commercial consequences that affect distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Home media completeness and edits
rubrics_metrics.description: DVD/home-video release practices are used to judge archival integrity: earliest releases included syndicated (shorter) versions of episodes due to rights issues; later re-releases rectified some problems. Seasons 8 and 9 remain edited (some scenes altered or missing) to avoid music-rights disputes; other regional releases (e.g., Germany) were mostly unedited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Completeness (uncut original broadcasts) versus edited/syndicated versions is an evaluative criterion for home media quality. Notes about substituted closing-credit scenes, missing footage, and region-specific differences illustrate how rights and licensing affect the integrity of released content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spin-off production conditions and rights/control
rubrics_metrics.description: When considering a spin-off (The Conners) after cancellation, the article notes it could only go forward if Roseanne Barr signed a deal to give up rights to the show so she would not be involved creatively or financially; she would likely receive a one-time payment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal/ownership and creative-control considerations are practical production criteria determining whether and how a series can be re-tooled or continued without its original creator. The requirement for rights transfer and removal of creative involvement are highlighted as conditions for proceeding with a spinoff.
